I now understand the disagreement fully.

**The bug:** `HeaderTickspeedRowModern` renders the AD Tickspeed lines unconditionally, whereas everywhere else in the game (the Classic header row and the Modern AD-tab `TickspeedRow`) gates tickspeed display on `Tickspeed.isUnlocked || EternityChallenge(9).isRunning`. On a fresh save the 2nd Antimatter Dimension hasn't been bought, so tickspeed isn't unlocked — Classic correctly shows nothing, Modern wrongly shows the tickspeed row.

The constraint is a trap-guard: the Classic row (`HeaderTickspeedRowClassic`) carries the actual **Tickspeed buy / Buy Max buttons**, while the Modern row has none. So "agreement" must not be achieved by unifying onto the button-less Modern component (that would strip a control Classic players reach). The correct fix is to add the same visibility gate to the Modern row, leaving Classic untouched. `GameSpeedDisplay` self-gates and stays.

steps.message:
The fix is complete.

## What was wrong

Both screenshots are the header center region of a freshly started save. The Modern theme showed an extra tickspeed block:

```
AD Tickspeed: 1.000 / sec
×1.125 faster per upgrade
```

…that the Classic theme did not. On a fresh save, tickspeed isn't unlocked yet (`Tickspeed.isUnlocked` requires the 2nd Antimatter Dimension to have been bought). Everywhere else in the game — the Classic header row (`HeaderTickspeedRowClassic`) and the Modern AD‑tab `TickspeedRow` — gates the tickspeed display on `Tickspeed.isUnlocked || EternityChallenge(9).isRunning`. Only `HeaderTickspeedRowModern` rendered it unconditionally, so it leaked pre‑unlock info that Classic (correctly) hid.

## The fix

Added the same visibility gate to `HeaderTickspeedRowModern.vue`: it now computes `isVisible` in `update()` and only renders the two tickspeed lines when tickspeed is actually unlocked. `GameSpeedDisplay` stays rendered — it already self‑gates and is empty on a fresh save — so nothing else changes. Now both themes show identical content at every progress point: nothing extra before unlock, tickspeed info after.

## Why not the other direction

The Classic row carries the real **Tickspeed buy / Buy Max buttons**; the Modern row has none. So "make them agree" could *not* mean collapsing both onto the button‑less Modern component or dropping Classic's gate — that would strip or alter a control Classic players can currently reach. I left `HeaderTickspeedRowClassic` completely untouched and only tightened Modern to match the game's existing unlock rule, so no reachable Classic control was affected.

`eslint` passes clean on the changed file.
